children: China's yuan was flat against the dollar on Tuesday, as traders wait for U.S. inflation data to be released this week for clues of the Federal Reserve’s rate path.
Meanwhile China’s export data for August is supporting the yuan's strength even as authorities’ guidance limits the upside.
“The yuan remains strong, but the pace of appreciation will likely be slow and steady," Huatai Futures said in a note, citing policymakers’ aversion to one-way currency bets.
In China's onshore market on Tuesday, the yuan
, changed hands at 6.7110 per dollar around midday, barely changed from the previous day’s close. It hit a 3-1/2-year high against the dollar on Monday.
The dollar index
slipped 0.06%.
All eyes are on the upcoming U.S. inflation data that could shape expectations for the Fed's next policy move.
The U.S. producer price index data is due on Thursday, and the consumer price index data is scheduled for Friday.
"The August data are a central input to the Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) decision on whether to hold or hike interest rates at the September policy meeting,” ANZ said in a note.
According to the CME FedWatch Tool, traders currently see a 60% chance of a rate hike at the Fed's policy meeting next week.
A U.S. rate hike would further widen the U.S.-China yield spread and rein in the yuan's rise.
But traders see further yuan strength underpinned by China's still-robust exports.
Fresh data on Tuesday showed China's export growth picked up pace last month, jumping 25% from a year earlier.
"The force bolstering the yuan is getting clear – exporters settling dollar receipts,” Huatai Futures said.
However, recent guidance by the People’s Bank of China signals policymakers’ intention toward the yuan's “steady strengthening, and two-way volatility.”
Prior to market open, the PBOC set the yuan’s midpoint
at 6.7804, 700 pips weaker than Reuters' forecast
, nearly the biggest deviation since February.
